title: Lower bound on check failure probability
statement: Let $m$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $2m$, and let $p$ be a Boolean string of length $2m+1$. Choose a seed uniformly from the $2m+2$ seeds consisting of two endpoint checks and, for each $i=0,\ldots,m-1$, two transition checks. A seed check holds when its endpoint bit has the required value, its product bit equals the conjunction of the corresponding two bits of $w$, or its prefix bits satisfy the stated recurrence modulo $2$, as appropriate. If at least one seed check fails, then the probability that a uniformly chosen seed fails is at least $1/(2m+2)$.
hypotheses_covered: There is a seed whose check fails
